text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The paper quotes unnamed sources from the central bank as saying the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) would support a reduction of interbank money market rates to around 15 percent.
- The NBS said it did not plan to implement any new administrative measures to strengthen its monetary policy.
- The majority of Slovak banks expect greater volatility in money market rates.
- State-owned Slovak railways estimate losses caused by the recent Czech rail strike at some 50 million crowns. The transport ministry said it would demand compensation from the Czech government.
- A group of companies linked to steel producer VSZ and the firm itself hold about 30 percent in the largest insurer Slovenska Poistovna.
- More than 621,000 people worked in Slovak industry last year, 445,000 of whom were employed in the private sector.
- Insulation producer Izomat plans to invest about 107 million crowns into modernisation programmes this year.
NARODNA OBRODA - German gas distributor Ruhrgas said it wanted to deliver western European gas to Slovakia.

- The ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), a junior member of the ruling coalition government, said it would again vote against bank privatisation but that it would not support attempts to call early elections. Another minor coalition partner, the Slovak National Party (SNS), has said early elections were the only way to solve current political problems.

- The state Institute for Agricultural Development and Economy of said preventing foreign capital from entering Slovakia's food industry was a mistake that made it difficult for Slovak producers to gain a foothold on foreign markets.
PRAVDA - Talks between the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) and the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) will take place within the next four weeks.
